terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where try.js starts the API on data/kilnworth.db and sends it a few reads.

tasks.title: List the workshops from the table
tasks.description:
Implement `list()` in `createStore(db)` in `src/store.js`, for now without filters. It returns every row of the `workshops` table as `{ id, title, day, seats, priceCents }`, in id order, and the query itself says that order.

The check fills a database of its own, sends `GET /workshops` and reads the SQL your store hands the database.
nextSteps: Write the `SELECT` with the five columns.
Say the order the rows come back in.
Run it with the method that gives back every row, and return what it gives.
hints: The route already sends whatever `list` returns, so `list` only has to give back the rows.
`ORDER BY id` puts the rows in id order. `.all()` gives back an array with one object per row, and `.get()` only the first row.
`return db.prepare('SELECT id, title, day, seats, priceCents FROM workshops ORDER BY id').all()`.

tasks.title: Read one workshop by its id
tasks.description:
Implement `get(id)` in `src/store.js`. It returns the workshop whose `id` is `id`, as `{ id, title, day, seats, priceCents }`, or `undefined` when there is no such row. The id reaches the database in the place of a `?`, never inside the SQL text.

The check sends `GET /workshops/:id` for ids that are in its table, one that is not and one that is not a number, and reads the SQL your store hands the database.
nextSteps: Write a `SELECT` with a `WHERE` on the id.
Leave a `?` where the id goes.
Run it with the method that gives back one row, handing it the id.
Run `node try.js` and look at the 404.
hints: The route answers 404 when `get` returns nothing, so a missing row has to come back as `undefined`, not as an empty list.
`.get(value)` fills the `?` with the value and gives back the first matching row, or `undefined`.
`return db.prepare('SELECT id, title, day, seats, priceCents FROM workshops WHERE id = ?').get(id)`.

videos.title: How text can change a SQL query

tasks.title: Filter in the query
tasks.description:
Make `list({ day, maxPriceCents })` in `src/store.js` use its filters. The route hands them over; one that was not asked for is `undefined`.

- `day` keeps the rows whose `day` is that day
- `maxPriceCents` keeps the rows whose `priceCents` is that much or less, and `0` is a real filter
- with both, a row has to match both; with neither, every row comes back

The database does the filtering: the query gives back only the rows in the answer. Each value reaches the database in the place of a `?`.

The check sends filtered lists, including a day that looks like SQL, counts the rows your query gives back and reads the SQL your store hands the database.
nextSteps: Start a list of conditions and a list of values.
Add a condition and its value for each filter that was given.
Put the conditions into the query only when there are any.
Hand the values to `.all()` and run `node try.js`.
hints: Only the pieces of SQL you write yourself may be joined into the query. What the visitor sent goes in the list of values.
Test each filter with `!== undefined`, so `0` counts. `conditions.join(' AND ')` joins the conditions, and `.all(...values)` hands the values over in order.
`if (day !== undefined) { conditions.push('day = ?'); values.push(day) }`, the same for `priceCents <= ?`, then `WHERE ${conditions.join(' AND ')}` before `ORDER BY id` when there are conditions.
